# h3-quinn 0.0.10 pending-read cancellation ownership fix

The published MIT-licensed h3-quinn 0.0.10 archive is vendored unchanged except
for `src/lib.rs`; this document and `regression/` are additions. Archive SHA-256
matches the previous workspace lock checksum:

`8b2e732c8d91a74731663ac8479ab505042fbf547b9a207213ab7fbcbfc4f8b4`

Published upstream revision: `2dc3412bdf6083451920d5bfd7a9484d054c1859`.
The workspace path patch selects this copy and only the h3-quinn registry
source/checksum are removed from the production lock. Dependency versions and
features are retained, including the now-unused tokio-util dependency so this
fix does not alter the resolved production graph.

## Failure and fix

Previously `poll_data` moved the receive stream into a stored owning future.
When that read returned Pending, `stop_sending` and `recv_id` unwrapped None.
HTTP/3 body cancellation during a pending read therefore panicked instead of
sending the request cancellation code to the peer.

`RecvStream` now always owns its native `quinn::RecvStream`. Each `poll_data`
creates a stack-pinned borrowed `read_chunk(usize::MAX, true)` future and polls
it once. That future is dropped when this poll returns; the stream stays
available for `stop_sending` and `recv_id`. This is a local ownership fix,
not a claim that an upstream release fixed it.

Quinn 0.11.11 explicitly documents `read_chunk` as cancel-safe. Its future's
poll delegates directly to private `poll_read_chunk`, which in turn performs
the native ordered chunk read and flow-control finalization. The future stores
only the borrowed stream and read arguments. Pending consumes no chunk and
registers the waker in the connection's blocked-reader table; recreating the
borrowed future on the next poll replaces that waker normally. No copied read,
custom stream parser, unsafe code, Quinn fork, or stored ownership future is
needed. `stop_sending` still calls native `stop` with the supplied VarInt;
Quinn discards unread data, releases flow control, removes the blocked reader,
and wakes its connection. Reset/connection error conversion is unchanged.

Primary sources:

- [Published h3 source revision](https://github.com/hyperium/h3/blob/2dc3412bdf6083451920d5bfd7a9484d054c1859/h3-quinn/src/lib.rs)
- [Quinn 0.11.11 receive implementation](https://github.com/quinn-rs/quinn/blob/quinn-0.11.11/quinn/src/recv_stream.rs)

## Targeted regressions

Run from the production workspace directory:

```sh
cargo test --manifest-path vendor/h3-quinn/regression/Cargo.toml
```

The isolated unpublished regression workspace pins the production Quinn, h3,
and rustls versions. It creates real loopback endpoints and an ephemeral test
certificate that the client explicitly trusts. It first sends and consumes a
prefix, leaving the sender open so the next receive poll must return Pending.
The four tests exercise:

1. ID access after Pending, another pending poll, resumed ordered data and EOF.
2. Stop after Pending, the exact H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED code observed by the peer,
   stable ID, Quinn's post-stop EOF, repeat stop and drop.
3. Peer reset after Pending, preserving the application error code.
4. Direct drop after Pending, preserving Quinn's implicit stop code zero.

Unpatched h3-quinn is expected to panic in the first two tests; the stop test
calls stop before querying the ID to independently cover the reproduced panic.
The certificate-generation dependencies exist only in the regression workspace.
Its lockfile may be generated by the coordinator on the first test run. This
worker is prohibited from running builds/tests; no runtime result is claimed.
The coordinator must run these regressions, affected core/Android builds and
live cancellation gates before release.
